scope: SQLite official WebAssembly/JavaScript documentation (api-index, persistence, npm, building) and 3.53.0 release notes

claims.claim: The sqlite3 WASM/JS API is exposed in several variants: sqlite3.capi (a wrapper over the C API), oo1 (the object-oriented API), Worker1 (a dedicated worker), and a virtual-table helper
OPFS is available only in Worker-thread contexts, not the main UI thread
Persistent/session storage options include kvvfs (localStorage/sessionStorage), JsStorageDb, opfs, opfs-wl, opfs-sahpool, WAL mode with OPFS, and OPFS over WASMFS
claims.notes: The earlier chapter's three-row VFS table was incomplete

claims.claim: The opfs-wl VFS was added in 3.53.0; it works like opfs but uses Web Locks instead of a bespoke protocol, requires Atomics.waitAsync(), shares over 90% of its code with opfs, has an OO1 wrapper sqlite3.oo1.OpfsWlDb, and shows no clear performance winner over opfs
For multi-tab concurrency use opfs or opfs-wl; clients that value performance over concurrency, or cannot set COOP/COEP headers, should use opfs-sahpool
The project is distributed as the npm module @sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm, with prerelease snapshots updated periodically
OPFS VFS has a caveat for Safari versions before 17 and depends on COOP/COEP HTTP headers in some configurations
claims.locator: Caveat: Safari versions < 17 / COOP/COEP HTTP Headers

claims.claim: The WASM build uses the Emscripten toolchain; build specifics are documented in the project's building/emscripten pages
claims.notes: The earlier chapter's exact emcc flags and ext/wasm file listing/line counts were removed as unverifiable
